podcast.body: Paul McCartney was chosen by co-producer Albert Broccoli to write the theme song for the 1973 James Bond film "Live and Let Die." McCartney reportedly wrote the song in about a day after reading a copy of the book and recorded it within a week during sessions for his "Red Rose Speedway" album at Air Studios. Producer George Martin insisted that McCartney's version be used as the title sequence, leading to its inclusion despite initial producer hesitancy. The song became a major worldwide hit, despite some "tortured grammar" in its lyrics. "Albert Broccoli had this idea of getting Paul McCartney to write the song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Sir Paul McCartney read an "e-inflaming novel" to better understand James Bond the night before he wrote this song, which served as the theme for the James Bond film "Live and Let Die." The song was a significant hit independently of the movie. "Live and Let Die would have been a hit without the movie."

This song was covered by Guns N' Roses in 1992, becoming their third hit to miss the top 20 and signaling the end of their imperial phase. "By the time their cover of Paul McCartney's Live and Let Die became their third hit to miss the top 20 in 1992, you could call the time of death."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
